title: Ezekiel Made a Watchman

questions.question: What did God tell Ezekiel to do with the scroll he found?
options: "Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."
"Read this scroll aloud in the city square."
"Burn this scroll as an offering."
"Hide this scroll until the appointed time."
questions.correctAnswer: "Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:1 (ESV): "And he said to me, 'Son of man, eat whatever you find here. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel.'"

questions.question: When Ezekiel ate the scroll containing lamentation and woe, how did it taste in his mouth?
options: As sweet as honey
As bitter as wormwood
Like dry ash
Like fresh bread
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:3 (ESV): "And I ate it, and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey."

questions.question: God told Ezekiel he was NOT being sent to a people of foreign speech and a hard language, but to whom?
options: The house of Israel
The Babylonians
The Egyptians
The remnant in Moab
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:5 (ESV): "For you are not sent to a people of foreign speech and a hard language, but to the house of Israel—"

questions.question: If God had sent Ezekiel to a people with a hard language, what did God say they would have done?
options: They would have listened to him
They would have killed him immediately
They would not have understood him
They would have mocked him
questions.correctAnswer: They would have listened to him
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:6 (ESV): "Surely, if I sent you to such, they would listen to you."

questions.question: Why will the house of Israel refuse to listen to Ezekiel?
options: Because they are not willing to listen to the Lord
Because they do not respect his age
Because he is not a true prophet
Because they are afraid of the Babylonians
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are not willing to listen to the Lord
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:7 (ESV): "But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me:"

questions.question: What is the condition of the house of Israel?
options: They all have a hard forehead and a stubborn heart
They are blind and deaf to the truth
They are lost sheep without a shepherd
They are seeking God but cannot find Him
questions.correctAnswer: They all have a hard forehead and a stubborn heart
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:7 (ESV): "because all the house of Israel have a hard forehead and a stubborn heart."

questions.question: What did God make Ezekiel's face and forehead like?
options: Like emery harder than flint
Like a radiant sun
Like a sharpened sword
Like a bronze wall
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:9 (ESV): "Like emery harder than flint have I made your forehead. Fear them not, nor be dismayed at their looks, for they are a rebellious house."

questions.question: Where did the Spirit lift Ezekiel and take him?
options: To the exiles at Tel-abib, who were dwelling by the Chebar canal
To the temple in Jerusalem
To the king's palace in Babylon
To a high mountain overlooking Judah
questions.correctAnswer: To the exiles at Tel-abib, who were dwelling by the Chebar canal
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:15 (ESV): "And I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who were dwelling by the Chebar canal,"

questions.question: How long did Ezekiel sit overwhelmed among the exiles at Tel-abib?
options: Seven days
Forty days
Three days
One month
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:15 (ESV): "and I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days."

questions.question: At the end of seven days, what title did God give Ezekiel?
options: A watchman for the house of Israel
A shepherd of the flock
A light to the nations
A judge over the people
questions.correctAnswer: A watchman for the house of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:17 (ESV): "Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel."

questions.question: If God tells Ezekiel "You shall surely die" to a wicked person, and Ezekiel does not warn them, what happens?
options: That wicked person shall die in his iniquity, but his blood God will require at Ezekiel's hand
Ezekiel is forgiven, but the wicked person dies in his iniquity
God finds another prophet to warn them
The plague will strike Ezekiel's house instead
questions.correctAnswer: That wicked person shall die in his iniquity, but his blood God will require at Ezekiel's hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:18 (ESV): "that wicked person shall die for his iniquity, but his blood I will require at your hand."

questions.question: What happens if Ezekiel does warn the wicked person, but they do not turn from their wickedness?
options: He shall die for his iniquity, but Ezekiel will have delivered his soul
Ezekiel must warn him three times before he is clean
God will spare the person because Ezekiel tried
Ezekiel will be punished for failing to convince him
questions.correctAnswer: He shall die for his iniquity, but Ezekiel will have delivered his soul
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:19 (ESV): "he shall die for his iniquity, but you will have delivered your soul."

questions.question: What happens if a righteous person turns from righteousness and commits injustice, and God lays a stumbling block before him, and Ezekiel does not warn him?
options: He shall die, his righteous deeds shall not be remembered, and his blood God will require at Ezekiel's hand
His righteous deeds will save him in the end
God will simply test him further
Ezekiel's soul is not held responsible since the person knew better
questions.correctAnswer: He shall die, his righteous deeds shall not be remembered, and his blood God will require at Ezekiel's hand
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:20 (ESV): "he shall die... his righteous deeds that he has done shall not be remembered, but his blood I will require at your hand."

questions.question: What instruction did God give Ezekiel when he went out into the valley?
options: "Go, shut yourself within your house."
"Build an altar out of stones."
"Gather the elders and speak to them."
"Pack your bags like an exile."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:24 (ESV): "Then the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet, and he spoke with me and said to me, 'Go, shut yourself within your house.'"

questions.question: God told Ezekiel that He would make his tongue cling to the roof of his mouth, so that he would be what?
options: Mute and unable to reprove them
Continually singing praises
Speaking in tongues
Paralyzed with fear
questions.correctAnswer: Mute and unable to reprove them
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 3:26 (ESV): "And I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, so that you shall be mute and unable to reprove them, for they are a rebellious house."

key_verse_text: "Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you shall give them warning from me."
